sections.html:
Up in north central Iowa, rural Wright County is governed from Clarion, the county seat and Eagle Grove is the largest city. The Boone and Iowa rivers cross it, and its neighbors are Hancock, Cerro Gordo, Franklin, Hardin, Hamilton, Webster, Humboldt and Kossuth counties. The county was organized in January 1851.

The 2020 census counted 12,943 residents, roughly 22 people per square mile, and an estimate for 2025 reads 12,801. Eagle Grove had 3,601 people, Clarion 2,810 and Belmond 2,463, with smaller towns including Goldfield, Dows, Woolstock, Rowan and Galt. Of 5,404 occupied households in 2020, 71.4 percent were owner-occupied.

For 2019 to 2023 the median owner-occupied home is valued at $109,800, and owners live in 74.2 percent of homes. There were 6,276 housing units in 2023. Typical gross rent is $788 and typical household income $64,033.

With a median home valued near $110,000, a repair estimate that looks small in a bigger market can weigh heavily here. Buyers in Clarion, Eagle Grove or Belmond often measure repair costs closely against price.

Clarion became the county seat in 1866, after the seat had been at Liberty since 1858. The courthouse dates from 1891 and 1892 and joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1981. Clarion had 2,810 residents in 2020, down from 2,968 in 2000.

Cold winters bring a January average high of 25.8 degrees F and 31.1 inches of snow a year, which puts roofs, insulation and furnaces under buyer scrutiny.

Employment leans toward food production and farm equipment. Clarion has an egg carton plant, Clarion Packaging, and Hagie Manufacturing, which builds high-clearance sprayers.

  • Prestage Foods of Iowa, a pork plant near Eagle Grove, had hired about 500 people by 2019, and a 2019 report said it spurred a housing construction boom in Eagle Grove and nearby towns.
  • The county bought 80 acres for an Agribusiness Park near Iowa Highway 17, and Ennis Corp. opened a washout business there in March 2021.
  • Iowa Specialty Hospital in Clarion employs about 450 people.

Eagle Grove has opened a housing district on its southeast side with lots for sale, which adds new construction to the competition for resale houses. Sellers in smaller towns such as Goldfield, Dows or Woolstock have fewer comparable sales for buyers to look at, so pricing is harder and sales can take longer.

Wright County has six active school districts, including Clarion-Goldfield-Dows, Eagle Grove and Belmond-Klemme. Clarion-Goldfield-Dows took its current form when Dows joined on July 1, 2014. The Eagle Grove district serves about 836 students across Wright, Humboldt and Webster counties. Iowa Central, North Iowa Area and Ellsworth community colleges are the nearest.

The Wright County Courthouse, 115 North Main Street in Clarion, houses the county offices from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Call (515) 851-0202 for the main line.

  • Treasurer: 515-532-2691, PO Box 226.
  • Assessor: 515-532-3737, PO Box 428.
  • Recorder: 515-532-3204, PO Box 187.
  • Auditor: 515-532-2771.

You can pay online at iowatreasurers.org and search property records on the county's Beacon site.

The assessor takes homestead applications on Form 54-028, due July 1. House File 718, signed May 4, 2023, created a further exemption for owners who turn 65 by January 1 of the assessment year.

It cuts taxable value by $3,250 for 2023 assessments and by $6,500 from the assessment year beginning January 1, 2024 on. Once granted it continues without refiling, as long as the owner still qualifies.

Data collectors visit properties during reviews and leave a door tag reading either "no action necessary" or "please contact our office." Under Iowa Code 441.37 the Board of Review accepts protests from April 2 through April 30. Call the assessor at 515-532-3737 about the current assessment year and any county notice.

Wright County taxes come due September 1 and March 1, and 1.5 percent monthly interest starts accruing October 1 and April 1. Most sales prorate the year at closing, crediting the buyer with the seller's portion.

Iowa Code 428A.3 puts the transfer tax on the seller: 80 cents per $500 over the first $500. Until it is paid, a taxable deed is not recorded.

Each June the courthouse hosts the tax sale, and bids are placed online at iowataxauction.com. Parcels are listed beforehand in the Wright County Independent in Belmond.

  • Redeeming a parcel adds 2 percent per month on the amount paid, and a partial month counts as a full one.
  • After 1 year and 9 months (regular sale) or 9 months (public bidder sale), a 90-day notice of right of redemption may be issued.
  • Certificate fee: $20. Treasurer's deed fee: $25 per parcel.
  • A certificate is canceled when no affidavit of service is filed within three years of the sale.

Own a parcel that was sold at the tax sale? Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure before arranging a sale.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call us
sections.html:
Have the deed, the most recent tax statement and any mortgage payoff figure ready. If you filed a homestead application, mention it, because the credit stops applying once you no longer live in the house. If the house sits in a town such as Eagle Grove, where a new housing district is adding lots, tell us what condition it is in so the offer reflects what buyers can get elsewhere.

Clear title moves the closing along. If a relative's name is still on the deed or an estate is involved, ask the recorder at 515-532-3204 what records exist, and expect an attorney to help sort out who can sign. None of this stops a cash sale, but it sets the schedule. The sale closes at a title company, and you can ask for the payoff and net amount in writing before you sign anything.

sections.h2: Before you sell a Wright County house
sections.html:
Renovating first is not always worth it; a house needing work can be simpler to sell as it stands. We make offers on Wright County houses in any condition, delinquent taxes included. Send the address and the newest tax statement for a written offer.

After you agree, a title company confirms ownership and asks for payoff figures. Closing pays taxes and liens first, then sends the remainder to you.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Wright County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Clarion. The courthouse is at 115 North Main Street, and Eagle Grove is the largest city.

faqs.q: When is the homestead credit deadline in Wright County?
faqs.a: Form 54-028 goes to the assessor by July 1. People 65 or older can also look into a separate House File 718 exemption.

faqs.q: How do I pay Wright County property tax?
faqs.a: Use iowatreasurers.org or call the treasurer at 515-532-2691. Installments fall on September 1 and March 1, and 1.5 percent monthly interest applies to late ones.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to redeem property sold at the Wright County tax sale?
faqs.a: The amount sold, plus 2 percent monthly (a partial month counts in full) and the $20 certificate fee. The treasurer can give an exact payoff.

faqs.q: Which Wright County town has the most people?
faqs.a: Eagle Grove, with 3,601 residents in 2020. Clarion followed with 2,810 and Belmond with 2,463.
